descriptionChirho: All four clusters represent the same noun metsad meaning 'stronghold' or 'fortress,' differing only in prepositions (be-/le-), number (singular vs plural), article, conjunction, and construct state. The multilingual evidence is uniform across all clusters: Arabic uses husun (حُصُونِ/حِصْن) throughout; Spanish uses 'fortalezas/fortaleza'; Korean uses yosae (요새/요새들); Hindi uses garh (गढ़/गढ़ों/गढ़ियाँ); Swahili uses ngome consistently. English glosses 'strongholds/stronghold' all denote a fortified defensive position.
